issue: #404 (CRUX audit E02) — the pre-apply drift gate opened one fresh SSH handshake per resource, before ControlMaster existed; no-op apply perf claims were false

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: `--plan-file` bypasses the hoist so its gate queries still handshake before any master exists — REFUTED: that path never runs the drift gate (apply_from_plan calls neither apply_pre_validate nor check_pre_apply_drift); the executor starts its own master before its first remote command, as always.
Sorting the locks by machine name makes the fan-out deterministic — REFUTED as worded: it fixes the order findings are collected and printed, not which machine answers first. Comment corrected.

Closing the --exclude/--skip gap is a semantics call about whether the gate should report a locked resource whose declaration is gone (the first cut's commit message) — REFUTED: the apply gate records drift THIS RUN will repair, and a resource the executor cannot touch is out of scope by the fix's own principle. Decided, implemented, pinned by gate_is_scoped_by_exclude.
quorum.divergence: the probe lane confirmed the hoist and the fan-out; the agy lane found the hoist opened masters to the WHOLE fleet under -r/-t/-g and that the fan-out was unbounded with first-error short-circuit — three of its five charges were taken, two refuted against the code.

systems: Ansible — ControlPersist via the ssh client; connections opened lazily against the FILTERED inventory, bounded by forks
Salt-SSH — opens per target as execution demands, from a bounded worker pool
pyinfra / Fabric — connect on the first remote operation against a specific host, never to hosts the run will not touch
Terraform SSH provisioner — one connection per provisioned resource, scoped to that resource
crux.verdict: nothing surveyed connects to hosts it will not use or runs unbounded. The first cut was below that bar on both counts; masters-by-scope and waves of 32 bring the gate to it.

agy_teamwork.verdict: REJECTED the first cut on five charges: fleet-wide masters under -r/-t/-g, --exclude unscoped, unbounded fan-out with first-error short-circuit, a duplicated gate predicate, and --plan-file. The first four were correct and are taken; --plan-file was refuted (that path runs no gate).
unique_findings: with -r/-t/-g the hoist opened a ControlMaster to every SSH machine in the file — an O(fleet) setup cost for an O(1) apply — taken: masters only for machines hosting an in-scope declared resource
r? on the first failing machine dropped the findings and errors of every machine after it — taken: every failure reported by name

pmat.quality_gate: no touched path in the vacuous or conditional-skip lists; clippy -D warnings 0 errors; fmt clean

falsification.test: reverted each production hunk in turn with the tests kept: the orphan-scope arm of GateScope::covers; the machines_in_scope narrowing (back to -m only); and, from the first cut, the group threading, the machine.rs socket-ownership hunk, and all of src/
falsification.reverted: src/cli/apply_drift.rs covers(): undeclared id -> `tag.is_none() && group.is_none()`; src/cli/apply_mux.rs ssh_machines_in_scope -> filter on scope.machine only; src/core/executor/machine.rs `Ok(started) => started` -> `Ok(_) => true`; group threading; all of src/
falsification.observed_failure: orphan arm reverted: gate_is_scoped_by_exclude RED (the gate probed alpha-b, which --exclude alpha-b excluded; lock came back drifted). Narrowing reverted: resource_and_tag_filters_narrow_the_fleet RED (3 machines picked for a one-resource scope). machine.rs reverted: a_control_master_this_run_did_not_open_survives_the_apply RED. All of src/ reverted: 0 passed, 4 failed.
falsification.still_green_when_reverted: gate_fans_out_across_machines stays green when only the bound is removed — the bound changes concurrency, not the overlap the test measures; it is pinned by the wave size being a named constant, not by a test

evidence.redaction: no machine-local identity in this set; the falsification fleet uses TEST-NET-1 addresses
known_limits: `forjar drift` (cli/drift.rs) still fans out unbounded, drops a panicked worker silently, and is not scoped by --exclude; the same repairs apply there and are deliberately not widened into a #404 change.
The wave size (32) is a constant, not a flag; a fleet whose gate wants a different pool size cannot set one yet.
Proves the masters open before the gate and only for in-scope machines, on the shim; does not measure the 45x on real hosts in CI.
